svg.title: A viewport requests image and cell data in parallel
svg.desc: A schematic pan from A to B supplies the same primary-image rectangle to two side-by-side worker branches. Image workers reuse resident tiles, range-read and decode a missing all-channel tile, and paint each available tile independently. Cell workers first query complete group bounds. Candidate row and byte totals select the geometry projection when detail fits, or the centroid projection otherwise, before either read. The projected-row table illustrates the shared identity and complete cell bounds on the geometry branch, not a separate bounds-only read. Geometry is decoded and intersected with B; centroids are accumulated in a symbolic 64 by 64 array with omitted rows and columns. The same normalized cells i1 and i2 supply every bounds, outline and centroid panel. The image-only B patch and final viewport are exact schematic crops of top B. JavaFX accepts a cell snapshot only for current image I and sequence B, discarding the late A completion. Native annotations belong to the image hierarchy and draw independently. Separate pixel, accepted-cell and native-annotation paths feed the single shared viewport below both workers. Shapes, rows, tile colours and array values are illustrative, not measured data.
